title: Kenyan Ice Cream Platter
community: Urban Kenya — the hotel dessert for all ages
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Ice Cream Platter — a generous hotel-style selection of vanilla, mango, coconut, and passion fruit ice cream scoops, served with fresh tropical fruit coulis, toasted coconut, Kenyan honey, wafer biscuits, and a sprig of mint. The dessert that pleases every table.
longDesc: The Kenyan ice cream platter at a hotel is not an afterthought — it is a considered, beautifully presented spread of multiple flavours with local coulis that makes the familiar extraordinary.
steps: Pre-chill the serving platter in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Scoop all ice creams and sorbets onto the chilled platter.
Drizzle mango coulis over vanilla and coconut scoops.
Drizzle passion fruit coulis over mango sorbet.
Scatter toasted coconut over all scoops.
Arrange wafer biscuits and fresh fruit around the scoops.
chefTips: A pre-chilled platter gives you more time before the ice cream melts.
Scoop ice cream in advance and freeze on a tray — perfect presentation without rushing.
Drizzle sauces in a zigzag pattern for restaurant visual impact.
commonMistakes: Sauces poured too heavily — overwhelms the ice cream.
cookingScience: A chilled platter slows the rate of heat transfer from the room-temperature plate to the cold ice cream — the temperature differential between the pre-chilled plate and the ice cream is smaller, reducing the melting rate.
sustainabilityTips: Mango and passion fruit sorbets can be made from local seasonal fruit at its peak.
servedWith: As a shared dessert for the table
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed as a celebration dessert.
culturalNote: The Kenyan ice cream platter demonstrates the hotel kitchen's understanding that dessert is about joy and sharing — a platter that arrives at the table and produces immediate smiles, in any restaurant in the world.
